leaf.text: An alternate leaf, 4 to 10 inches long, with 5 to 7 bristle-tipped lobes and sinuses that range from deep to shallow. The upper side is shiny green; the lower side is paler with soft hairs.
leaf.ref: Virginia Tech Dendrology fact sheet, Quercus velutina (ID 39)

leaf.text: An opposite leaf, 3 to 6 inches long, with 5 rounded lobes and a smooth margin. The upper side is green; the lower side is paler.
leaf.ref: Virginia Tech Dendrology fact sheet, Acer saccharum (ID 2)

leaf.text: An alternate leaf, 6 to 12 inches long, with many lobes and two deep middle sinuses that almost reach the midrib. The lobes near the tip form a crown shape; the upper side is green and the lower side is paler and fuzzy.
leaf.ref: Virginia Tech Dendrology fact sheet, Quercus macrocarpa (ID 72)

leaf.text: An alternate leaf, 4 to 7 inches long, with 7 to 10 rounded, finger-like lobes and sinuses from deep to shallow. The upper side is green to blue-green; the lower side is whitish.
leaf.ref: Virginia Tech Dendrology fact sheet, Quercus alba (ID 35)

leaf.text: An alternate leaf, 4 to 8 inches wide, broadly ovate in shape, with 3 to 5 lobes and coarse, toothed margins. The veins may show fine hairs on the lower side.
leaf.ref: Virginia Tech Dendrology fact sheet, Platanus occidentalis (ID 36)
